rationale: B wins because it knows where the facts stop. A has sharper reporter targeting, but it keeps the overextended angle "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones," which imports a neobank-collapse thesis the update did not provide. B correctly refuses the same move as "Neobanks are failing, so the profitable ones are winning consumers" and keeps the founder out of the hallucination ditch.
gaps_in_A: "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones" is the big sin: the update says Mercury is profitable and entering consumer banking, not that consumer neobanking broke unprofitable players.

"The prevailing belief on this beat is that consumer neobanking is a customer-acquisition money pit" may be plausible industry context, but it is not in the supplied facts. You cannot smuggle a thesis in and call it grounding.
"now wants your paycheck" overreaches. The facts say checking and savings accounts, not direct deposit, payroll capture, or primary-account ambition.
"category-creation" is the wrong label for the partner-bank angle. Sponsor-bank consumer fintech is not a new category; the actual story is disclosure, deposit custody, and supervision.
gaps_in_B: "The startup bank" is sloppy shorthand for a company whose own structure angle says it is not a chartered bank. Cute headline, but precision matters here.
"fintech-strategy reporter" and "strategy newsletter writer" are usable but softer than they should be. The set needs tighter sub-beats, not broad desk fog.

It leaves a strong SVB trust-transfer story underdeveloped. "grew up after SVB" becomes color inside a competitive angle instead of a clean business-news question about whether crisis-era trust travels to retail deposits.
"Next step: meanest-editor" is the wrong operational handoff for an angle set. The next move is to secure proof or run journalist-fit-check, not roast a pitch that does not exist yet.
